mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium as investors anticipate future rate hikes, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 5-day rolling average during similar inflation spikes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly PAYEMS labor cost growth above 0.5% for two consecutive months signals wage pressures that prompt equity market anticipation of higher profits, producing positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases for two consecutive months and exceeds 0.5% in the second month
failure_condition: During analogous wage acceleration episodes, 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in GDPC1 personal consumption expenditures exceeding 2% of the prior month's value, accompanied by a simultaneous decline in RSAFS inventories, predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as demand recovers.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > GDPC1 previous * 1.02 AND RSAFS < RSAFS previous
failure_condition: In analogous demand-recovery episodes, the 20-day forward return does not exceed the 5-day average by more than one standard deviation (IC > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO supply index falling below 96.0 while HOUST industrial production remains flat for two months indicates softening supply constraints, which is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 96.0 AND HOUST >= HOUST previous AND HOUST current == HOUST previous
failure_condition: During comparable supply-side softening, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in FEDFUNDS below 1.0% for three consecutive months, absent a concurrent inflation spike in CPIAUCSL, predicts negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors anticipate recessionary financing conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1.0 for three consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 0.2 for the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 5-day forward returns during similar rate declines are not significantly negative (IC > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in UNRATE unemployment rate below 5.0% for two consecutive months indicates labor market weakness that precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as risk aversion increases.
failure_condition: During comparable unemployment declines, 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A one-time monthly spike in PAYEMS labor costs exceeding 2.5% above the prior month's level, without a corresponding rise in GDP signals wage-driven demand shock that produces a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > PAYEMS previous * 1.025 AND GDPC1 < GDPC1 previous
failure_condition: In analogous wage shock events, the 20-day forward return does not beat the 5-day average by more than one IC standard deviation (IC > 0.12).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO supply index of at least 1.0% for four consecutive months in a non-recession regime is associated with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates supply disruption risks.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < INDPRO previous * 0.99 for four consecutive months AND GDP growth > 0.5% in the current month
failure_condition: During similar supply declines in non-recession months, 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).
